## Ethics Statement {.unnumbered}

This study generated no new human or animal material. It reanalyzes anonymous human sequencing data from the open-access tiers of the NCBI Sequence Read Archive and the European Nucleotide Archive; no library was held under controlled access. We used no identifiable private information, did not attempt to re-identify participants, and used no individual-level data beyond each record's own archive annotation. Anonymous data fall outside the material scope of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (Article 2, Recital 26), which does not cover anonymous information even when it is processed for research. The work involved no human subjects, so it required no ethics committee review or participant consent, and none was sought. Approval and consent for the original collection were the submitting investigators' responsibility; no archive record states whether that consent covered secondary use, which anonymous data do not require.

<!-- TP's decision, 2026-11-02, on the round-3 review package: rest the exemption on
     GDPR Article 2 with Recital 26 and call the data "anonymous" throughout, in
     place of the unattributed basis the earlier draft asserted. The two must move
     together: Recital 26 exempts anonymous information only, so citing it while
     calling the data "de-identified" would concede the point it is cited to make.

     The risk, if a reviewer or editor queries it: "anonymous" is a stronger
     characterisation than "de-identified", and raw human sequencing reads are widely
     treated as personal data even stripped of identifiers, so this asserts a legal
     conclusion about genomic data rather than describing the files. The supporting
     facts, which the sentence states, are that every deposit is open access rather
     than controlled, and that we used no individual-level information beyond the
     archive's own sample annotation.

     Still worth doing before submission: confirm the position with the University of
     Tartu Research Ethics Committee. Some journals ask for a waiver in writing, and
     a confirmation costs nothing. -->

## Data Availability Statement {.unnumbered}

The complete analysis pipeline, comprising the Nextflow workflow, the per-process software environments and container definitions, the reference-construction and SRA-discovery scripts, and the downstream R analysis and statistical-inference code, is openly available at <https://github.com/tpall/hpv-human-skin>. All sequencing data analyzed here are public and were obtained from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive; the per-cohort lists of accessions (SRR/SRX), with assigned tissue category, diagnosis, and cell-line/engineered annotations, are provided as Supplementary Data. A further table (`supplementary_data_unscreened_libraries.tsv`, built by `bin/build_unscreened_table.py`) lists every library that entered the prevalence sweep but returned no screening result, with its cause, so the positivity denominator can be reconstructed from the accession lists. A second Supplementary Data table (`supplementary_data_ethics_provenance.tsv`) gives, for each source study contributing a lesion or neoplasia library, the study and BioProject accession, a direct link to the archive record, the diagnoses represented, the originating publication where one could be identified, and that publication's approval and consent statements where it reports them; the scripts that compiled it from the public archive and Europe PMC records are in `manuscript/ethics_audit/` in the repository above. Reference genomes were retrieved from the Papillomavirus Episteme (PaVE; <https://pave.niaid.nih.gov>) and NCBI RefSeq. No new sequencing data were generated.
